items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: Dizzie Gillespie joined you at the famous Door... in a sextet I had.

ctx.x: Now you had come up and had been accustomed to playing in a certain way. But do you remember at the time any question of adjustment or Dizzie adjusting?
Well, the only thing that I recall was that Dizzie did his thing and I did my thing, and you know?
So far as you knew, youwere both concerned, you went very well together?

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: I made one with ... Dizzy Gillespie and I and the rhythm section

ctx.x: Yes, he played a chorus, I played a chorus on trumpet, Clark Terry, Claude Perry, Dizzy Gillespie, John Faddis, and ... is that 6? Dizzy Gillespie, Claude Perry, Clark Terry, Doc Cheatham, Faddis, Carter -- Faddis, Carter -- who was the other one? There was another one -- there were 6 of us. Harry Edison.

items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I’m looking forward to playing with Dizzy on his October cruise.

ctx.x: I think he replaced Dizzy briefly at some point.
That’s right. He replaced Dizzy later, yeah.
But it was still in the same small group.
